hints: At constant speed on a level track, acceleration is zero, so driving force equals resistance: $F_D = R$.
Use the power relation $P = F_D \times v$ with $P = 4080\text{ kW} = 4080000\text{ W}$ and $v = 85\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough:
State the force equilibrium along the level track at constant velocity ($a = 0$):
$$F_D = R$$
where $F_D$ is the engine driving force and $R$ is the resistive force.

State the formula relating driving force, power, and velocity:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v}$$
Convert power to watts: $P = 4080\text{ kW} = 4080000\text{ W}$.
Substitute $P = 4080000\text{ W}$ and $v = 85\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$R = \frac{4080000}{85} = 48000\text{ N}$$

hints: When ascending the incline at constant speed, the driving force must overcome both the resistance and the downhill component of weight: $F_D = R + mg\sin\alpha$.
Sum the forces to find the total driving force, then multiply by the speed $v = 85\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to find the power.
walkthrough:
State the force balance for uphill motion at constant speed ($a = 0$):
$$F_D - R - mg\sin\alpha = 0$$
$$F_D = R + mg\sin\alpha$$
where $R = 48000\text{ N}$ is the unchanged resistance force and $mg\sin\alpha$ is the component of gravity down the slope.

Substitute $m = 490000\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $\sin\alpha = \frac{1}{200}$:
$$mg\sin\alpha = 490000 \times 10 \times \frac{1}{200} = \frac{4900000}{200} = 24500\text{ N}$$
Compute the required driving force:
$$F_D = 48000 + 24500 = 72500\text{ N}$$

State the power formula:
$$P = F_D \times v$$
Substitute $F_D = 72500\text{ N}$ and $v = 85\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = 72500 \times 85 = 6162500\text{ W}$$
Convert to megawatts by dividing by $10^6$:
$$P = \frac{6162500}{1000000} = 6.1625\text{ MW} \approx 6.16\text{ MW}$$
